name: Cordon-Vitae
description: Cordon-Vitae is painfully lovely from orbit: jade forests climbing terraced mountains, rivers the color of milk-quartz braiding through canyon country, and cloud banks that glow gold at dawn. It is the kind of world colonists dream about, which is precisely why it is guarded like a wound.

On the ground the air is sweet and humid, thick with pollen that drifts in slow spirals through shafts of light. The silence is what unsettles visitors; there are no animal calls anywhere. Forests rustle, water runs, and nothing else moves unless it grew there.

The Halcyon Consortium built its gene-labs into an old mining complex in the basin canyons, engineering bespoke crops and pharmaceuticals from native flora. Nine years ago the Halcyon Strain crossed out of containment and into the wild biosphere, rewriting everything it touched; the fauna died within two seasons and the flora began expressing structures no botanist could classify. The Consortium's board was arrested, the labs were entombed in their own foundations, and the planet was placed under total biological quarantine.

Automated defense platforms still hold the high orbitals with live weapons authorization, and interdiction beacons repeat the same message on every band: approach is prohibited, landing is fatal to the ecosystem if not to you. Yet the engineered flora may hold cures worth fortunes, and every year a faster smuggler tests whether the platforms have finally been allowed to sleep.
